hypothesis: Y037 found a fixed bijective cell relabeling changes matching outcomes because native numeric tie-break is not coordinate invariant. Independently validate with four new invertible cell maps; inverse-canonical tie-break should reproduce original reference allocations under every map, not just the one from Y037.
freeze: Freeze four independent odd-multiplier bijections, offset formula, policies, seeds, exact canonical sort and classification criteria before original execution; no cherry-pick mappings.
graph: Exactly the frozen original ring_reference seven active / sixteen motifs-and-cells / 9 inactive retained / eight episodes, radius-two graph and augmenting-path matcher; no new neighbors or action space.
modes: reference_numeric: unswapped cell labels and numerical sorter
scrambled_numeric: permuted labels, same numerical sorter
scrambled_canonical: permuted labels, sorter uses bijection-inverse canonical cell ID, same preferred-first prioritization
primary: For 4 bijections x 3 policies x 16 heldout seeds x 8 episodes, record complete key-to-canonical-cell assignments, mismatch counts relative to corresponding reference at identical seed/episode/policy, heldout churn and cache writes.
classification: MULTI_MAP_TIEBREAK_CONFOUND if scrambled_canonical allocations exactly match reference under every permutation/seed/policy/episode, and scrambled_numeric differs under at least one permutation and changes aggregate churn for at least one policy. PARTIAL if canonical mismatches strictly fewer than scrambled numeric but nonzero. NO_CONFIRMED_CONFOUND otherwise.
controls: Independent Hall 7 bound per graph/episode and valid matching seven without repeated cells
Identical cache writes and key occupancy by corresponding policy, all modes
No future graph, hidden labels or extra action capacity; inverse relabel is known metadata of the experimental coordinate system, not an oracle
Original immutable SHA identities, first-use archive, one full regression, no accepted-ref mutation
claim_limit: Finite synthetic deterministic matcher-coordinate equivariance study, not evidence of learned semantic memory.
